text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The queue for health services is growing with 68,000 people now waiting for treatment. This is 6,700 more than a year ago.
- At least 2,000 jobs will be lost through the merger of Swedish banks Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announced on Tuesday. The new bank will be called ForeningsSparbanken.
- The battle between Swedish newspapers has stepped up with new readers being offered half price subscriptions.
- Sweden's second largest building company NCC has bought its competitor Siab. The acquisition was greeted positively by the market and the share prices of all parties involved rose on Tuesday.

- Swedish bus and truck maker Scania posted a worse result for 1996, saying it was a complicated year. Sales fell by three percent to 33.7 billion crowns while its profit after financial items slumped 44 percent to 2.71 billion crowns. The result was in line with expectations.
- Two Swedish mergers were announced on Tuesday with banks Swedbank and Foreningsbanken becoming a couple and construction and real estate companies NCC and Siab marrying.

- Foreningsbanken, Swedbank and Nordbanken presented earnings and Nordbanken's chief executive Hans Dalborg said 1996 was an extreme year with sharply lower bond yields boosting the bank's bond portfolio profits.
- Trygg-Banken, the bank set up by Swedish insurance company Trygg-Hansa in October 1995, on Tuesday bought the Swedish household operations of French bank Credit Lyonnais.

- Swedish banks Swedbank and Foreningsbanken are to merge creating Sweden's second biggest bank with combined assets of 619 billion crowns. On the same day record annual profits were announced by several Swedish banks. Swedbank chairman Goran Collert, who will take over as chairman of the merged bank, noted that an extensive network of local offices will remain even after planned cuts. The banks have office side-by-side in 220 locations.

- Insurer Trygg Hansa said its subsidiary Trygg-Banken is buying Credit Lyonnais Bank Sverige. The 12,000 private customers of the bank have deposits of 2.1 billion crowns. Credit Lyonnais will maintain a branch office in Sweden devoted to corporate clients.
- Building companies NCC and Siab said they will merge to create a construction and real estate group with a workforce of 23,000 and combined annual turnover of nearly 35 billion crowns.

- Chairman of the board of state-owned telephone company Telia said discussions about a privatisation were underway. Westerberg told Dagens Industri that the government has not resulted out privatising and listing Telia.
